description: Financial Services Data Model (FSDM) business glossary seeded from industry-standard definitions. Terms cover core financial domain concepts, data governance policies, and lakehouse architecture layers.

terms.name: Trade
terms.description: A financial transaction involving buying or selling a security, derivative, or other financial instrument. Trades have a trade date, settlement date, price, quantity, and counterparty. In the lakehouse, raw trade data arrives in the bronze layer and is standardized in silver.

terms.name: Position
terms.description: The amount of a security or financial instrument held by an entity at a specific point in time. A position is the net result of all trades in a given security. Can be long (owned) or short (borrowed and sold). Positions are tracked daily in the gold layer.

terms.name: Business Unit
terms.description: An organizational division or segment of the firm that operates with its own profit and loss responsibility. Common business units include Wealth Management, Investment Banking, Risk Management, and Retail Banking. Business units are used to partition data access and ownership in the lakehouse.

terms.name: PII
terms.description: Personally Identifiable Information -- any data that could be used to identify a specific individual. Subject to data protection regulations including GDPR, CCPA, and industry-specific rules. In the lakehouse, PII columns are automatically classified via regex rules and masked for non-privileged users.

terms.name: BCBS 239
terms.description: Basel Committee on Banking Supervision Principles for Effective Risk Data Aggregation and Risk Reporting (BCBS 239). Requires financial institutions to have strong risk data aggregation capabilities and internal risk reporting practices. The lakehouse supports BCBS 239 compliance through end-to-end data lineage tracking via OpenLineage/Marquez.

terms.name: Bronze Layer
terms.description: The first layer of the medallion architecture. Contains raw ingested data with minimal transformation -- primarily format conversion (e.g., CSV/JSON to Iceberg Parquet). Data in the bronze layer preserves the original source schema and values. Schema may reflect source system quirks. Retention: typically 7 years for regulatory compliance.

terms.name: Silver Layer
terms.description: The second layer of the medallion architecture. Contains cleansed, validated, and standardized data. Source-system quirks are resolved (e.g., date formats normalized, NULL handling applied), and FSDM schema conformance is enforced. Used for cross-source joins and analytical queries.

terms.name: Gold Layer
terms.description: The third layer of the medallion architecture. Contains business-ready aggregated data, denormalized for analytical consumption. Gold tables are optimized for BI tools, AI/ML features, and API consumption. These datasets represent the single, governed copy of truth for business metrics.

terms.name: Data Freshness
terms.description: The time elapsed since the last successful data update for a given dataset. Data freshness is tracked per table using traffic-light SLA status: GREEN (within expected interval), YELLOW (past warning threshold), RED (stale -- past critical threshold). Freshness dashboards are visible in Grafana and the OpenMetadata catalog.

terms.name: SLA
terms.description: Service Level Agreement for data delivery timeliness. Each dataset in the lakehouse has a defined SLA specifying the expected update interval and thresholds for warning (YELLOW) and critical (RED) status. SLA breaches trigger alerts via Grafana. Default SLAs: Gold 24h expected/48h critical, Silver 12h/24h, Bronze 6h/12h.

terms.name: notional_value
terms.description: The total dollar value of a trade or position, calculated as price multiplied by quantity. Notional value represents the gross market exposure for a given instrument. Used in trading dashboards for exposure reporting.

terms.name: trade_count
terms.description: The total number of individual trade executions in a given grouping (by symbol, side, time period). Trade count is a core activity metric used for volume analysis and operational reporting.

terms.name: average_price
terms.description: The mean execution price across all trades for a given instrument and side. Calculated as a weighted or simple average depending on context. Used for cost basis analysis and execution quality monitoring.

terms.name: market_value
terms.description: The current market value of a position, calculated as quantity multiplied by the current market price per unit. Market value represents the mark-to-market exposure for portfolio valuation and risk reporting.

terms.name: var_95
terms.description: Value at Risk at 95% confidence level. The maximum expected loss over a specified time horizon such that there is a 95% probability the actual loss will not exceed this amount. A core risk metric required by BCBS 239 for risk reporting.

terms.name: var_99
terms.description: Value at Risk at 99% confidence level. The maximum expected loss over a specified time horizon such that there is a 99% probability the actual loss will not exceed this amount. More conservative than VaR 95, used for stress testing and regulatory capital calculations.

terms.name: expected_shortfall
terms.description: Expected Shortfall (Conditional VaR) measures the average loss in the tail beyond the VaR threshold. Captures the severity of tail risk events. ES is considered a more coherent risk measure than VaR and is increasingly required by regulators.

terms.name: position_count
terms.description: The total number of open positions in a given grouping (by account, sector, currency). Used for portfolio concentration analysis, diversification monitoring, and capacity planning.
